740340101.text: ...I just can't believe it. Would someone really take a Kamera into the Maison Gestion itself, and simply strut about taking pictures of everyone and anything?

740340102.text: It is ridiculous! Everyone knows, everyone should know, that that is how secrets get leaked! It is common sense!

740340103.text: If common sense was common, Mr. Iaune, then the Maison Gestion could simply disband tomorrow.

740340104.text: I shall leave this to you. Have them sign the document, just like I taught you, and return it to me before the weekend.

740340105.text: I still have to handle the expense receipts. Carsix keeps hassling me about it.

740340106.text: But, Mr. Roialte, just who should I be looking for? We don't have an office specifically in charge of Kameras.

740340107.text: Uh... I trust your judgment. Now hurry up and take care of this, so we can each really enjoy the weekend! I'm going to go take care of other things. Hop to it, kid!

740340133.text: Roialte leaves in a leisurely manner...

740340110.text: Huh? Hello, hello. It looks, though, you are not a member of the staff here at the Maison Gestion.

740340111.text: I am currently busy with official business. Should you have any inquiries, please ask Ms. Cornelia. She's right over there.

740340112.text: She will provide you with a chair and a cup of tea. Please have a seat, and I will come find you after I am done.

740340114.text: *sigh* It's... It's actually a simple matter, but dealing with it is quite complicated...

740340115.text: The office I work in has received a notice instructing us to draft a letter to the other offices.

740340116.text: The content was something like, staff are forbidden from bringing Kameras into the Maison Gestion and taking pictures, except for work purposes, in order to avoid leakage of secret information.

740340117.text: Does telling me about the letter's contents constitute leaking secrets?

740340118.text: No, certainly not. If anyone really had used a Kamera to take a photo of documents, and it resulted in a leak, then this would certainly be a confidential matter.

740340119.text: However, "maybe someone will use a Kamera to take a picture of documents in order to leak them" is not a secret. After all, that's a possibility that everyone is aware of.

740340121.text: Think about it this way: If you are guarding a secret, then the secret you are guarding certainly cannot be revealed.

740340122.text: But the fact that "you are guarding a secret" itself may not be considered secret.

740340123.text: After all, if even the fact that "you are guarding a secret" is considered a secret, then you will fall into an endless cycle of keeping the secret of keeping secrets.

740340124.text: Your wording is an endless cycle!

740340127.text: That is where this matter becomes complicated. There is no office in the entire Maison Gestion that is directly charged with managing Kameras.

740340128.text: Mr. Semaine says that I should ask Mr. Gattineo. Their work is related to confidential matters, and thus they should be the first to be made aware.

740340129.text: But Mr. Roialte says that I should ask Difor, as he is in charge of all matters related to the staff of the Maison Gestion.

740340130.text: Were we to make a new rule that all staff of the Maison Gestion cannot bring Kameras to work, we'd have to let them know.

740340131.text: Wow... That's complicated... Why are there so many different people responsible for different things? What happens if you can't remember?

740340132.text: That's why each of us carries a thick notepad. Though even with the notes, I'm still not sure who I should look for now...

740340401.text: Well, I guess you'll get to see for yourselves. Please, this way.

740340201.text: This is a confidential matter. Let's look for Gattineo.

740340202.text: That's exactly what I thought. Mr. Gattineo is quite affable, and is also an "exemplary Gestionnaire."

740340203.text: Even though all the matters he deals with are of utmost importance, he still handles each matter with aplomb. His work can truly be called outstanding.

740340301.text: This is a matter involving personnel. Let's look for Difor.

740340302.text: That's exactly what I thought, but he has quite the explosive temper, and though he is quite reliable, his sharp tongue is sure to leave a mark.

740340303.text: *sigh* But he must be informed of this matter as soon as possible...

740340501.text: Iaune! What're the odds? Do you finally have time for a cup of coffee with me after work?

740340502.text: Thank you for your offer, but I have a confidential matter that requires your attention.

740340503.text: "Confidential matter"? Is it something I know about?

740340504.text: I think you may not have been informed yet. I only received the document this morning.

740340505.text: Now that's odd. Perhaps my information is a step behind yours since I haven't had a chance to read The Steambird yet today.

740340506.text: But it's a confidential matter. Why would you read about it in The Steambird?

740340507.text: Hahaha! Those reporters get information and spread it far faster than our internal memos here at the Maison Gestion can.

740340508.text: Of course, it's understandable. After all, they get paid when they deliver a message.

740340509.text: Paimon doesn't get it at all...

740340510.text: Let's not talk about that for now. Sir, it's like this...

740340511.text: Iaune explains the situation in detail...

740340512.text: Ha! That's right, such an announcement is absolutely necessary. This already happened. Some blithering idiot wanted to show off his desk layout, and took a picture of it.

740340513.text: He's a member of the Kamera Club, and showed that very photo to the other members of the club.

740340534.text: But one of the members of said club just happened to be an astute reporter, who quickly noticed a document that looked like an internal memo in the picture.

740340514.text: And guess what happened next? The next day, that blasted memo complaining that only fish gets served for dinner here, day in and day out, was all over The Steambird!

740340515.text: Does that count as a secret...?

740340517.text: Whatever it is, it's internal information, and it should not be leaked to any outside parties!

740340518.text: The people of the Court of Fontaine never miss an opportunity to mock and deride the Maison Gestion, and we must act with caution.

740340519.text: As if they actually gave two figs about what we actually do here! All they want to do is... ugh, have a laugh.

740340520.text: Uh, anyway... I'll leave this to your office to take care of, then...

740340521.text: But this matter concerns new rules for personnel... Difor is the one who should sign off on this.

740340522.text: After all, in this document, though it reminds everyone of the importance of keeping confidential information secret, the more important thing is how to communicate these principles to them.

740340523.text: If you ask me, it must be Difor that takes care of this. Our office will certainly assist in this matter. This will be more efficient, and confidentiality can be maintained.

740340524.text: Gattineo swiftly signs his name on the dotted line reading "co-organizer"...

740340526.text: Come on, boy! You can't dawdle about, this must be taken care of! Now go find Difor quickly, before his patience is worn thin by other matters.

740340527.text: Now, I'll go find some documents that talk about the principles of protecting secret information. When the document is ready to be officially promulgated, our office will provide our full support!

740340535.text: Go find him, kid! I've got to go... uh, attend to other matters.

740340531.text: There, did you see Mr. Gattineo's abilities? His secret to getting everything done so well is avoiding doing anything at all that carries even a modicum of risk.

740340532.text: Oh, so it's the ability to shirk your duties...

740340533.text: There's nothing we can do now... Except go find Mr. Difor. This way, please.

740340601.text: Do you have something for me, Iaune? You seem to be out of breath.

740340603.text: Iaune explains the situation in detail...

740340604.text: You've come to the wrong person, Iaune. This document clearly has the subject of "secrets." How could you fail to realize something so simple and obvious?

740340605.text: I thought the subject was "this document."

740340607.text: Hey, that's not the subject right now, either!

740340608.text: Your exactness is noted and appreciated. But I will not sign this document no matter what. I will not even entertain the thought! It should be Gattineo who leads this matter.

740340609.text: Mr. Gattineo said, you should be the one in charge...

740340610.text: Ha! ME? And how should I do it? Grab a megaphone and stand at the door, shouting at everyone as they come in to work?

740340611.text: "Hey! Ladies and Gentlemen, don't bring your Kameras to work! You'll leak all kinds of secrets! That would be bad, so don't!"

740340612.text: Or maybe print up a few hundred documents, and leave them on the desk of every Gestionnaire so they can take them with them as they go get their coffee?

740340613.text: You think we're like Gattineo? That we can just grab leakers and teach them a lesson? All we can do is send out notices, the kind nobody takes notice of!

740340614.text: But, he's already signed the document, look here...

740340615.text: Boy, do you have any clue what "co-organizer" means?

740340616.text: Um... the one who follows instructions from the other party?

740340617.text: It means "At least I'm not responsible for this."

740340618.text: I categorically and completely refuse to sign this document. If it must be my office that is forced to take charge of this, then let Maneval come down and tell me so in person!

740340619.text: Difor charges out in a rage...

740340620.text: H—He's so loud... Paimon didn't even dare to speak...

740340621.text: As I said, he has quite the temper.

740340622.text: So what do we do now?

740340623.text: Don't worry, let's just go back and look for Mr. Roialte.

740340701.text: Iaune! Let me guess. Bad news?

740340702.text: Sir, you are correct it is not good news. To be precise, it is "secret" news.

740340704.text: Very funny, Iaune. So what is this "secret" news?

740340705.text: Iaune explains the situation in detail...

740340706.text: That is true, something like this could easily happen. After all, most of the staff here at the Maison Gestion aren't very sensitive to how confidential different documents are.

740340709.text: It's all thanks to Gattineo and his people. All the documents here have to be reviewed by them. They decide the security classification of the document and stamp it.

740340710.text: Sounds like a good system, right? But the folks in charge of reviewing documents came up with a truly ingenious way to save time: just stamp "secret" on every single blasted document that comes their way!

740340711.text: Last week, Carsix went to the Opera Epiclese for a speech, and talked about recent performances.

740340712.text: I remember, it wasn't a long speech, and lots of people were there. The text of his speech was even in the newspapers.

740340713.text: Since the speech was given in front of everyone, and everyone knows it all already... how can something everyone knows be a secret?

740340714.text: But noooo, even so, Gattineo still just has to classify it as "secret."

740340801.text: Iaune! To think I'd meet you here, you little rascal.

740340802.text: Mr. Gattineo, I was just looking for you! There's something you should know...

740340803.text: What is it? I just finished reading today's Steambird, and the Maison Gestion wasn't mentioned.

740340804.text: Yes, this is a secret matter.

740340805.text: Oh, now that's a rare sight! Someone besides a journalist who can tell if something is secret or not.

740340806.text: Iaune explains the situation in detail...

740340807.text: *sigh* It appears our Difor is an exceptionally diligent journalist. It's almost as if he charged into my office demanding to know the security classification of this document.

740340808.text: I completely concur with his opinion. This matter certainly must be reviewed and classified first, but the matter of "Kamera Security Leaks" is quite large, and concerns the entire Maison Gestion.

740340809.text: My office alone cannot ascertain the confidentiality. I must go to the other offices first, and allow them to review it, and once they are all familiar with the matter, we then can proceed. For example... Carsix.

740340810.text: Huh? But this order came down from Mr. Carsix...

740340811.text: Then it is even more imperative that he be aware of how we are dealing with it. Come on, lad, let's go find Roialte, and then meet with Carsix.

740340901.text: This is a confidential matter. As such, it falls under your office's jurisdiction.

740340902.text: Well, in that case, can we keep affairs we handle confidential from you in the future — even on personnel-related matters?

740340903.text: Hey, those are two different things. Quit shifting the goalposts!

740340904.text: Well, it's certainly not up to us to decide whether or not they're the same thing!

740340905.text: It looks like... I've messed things up again...

740340908.text: #{NICKNAME}, how... How about we get out of here? Adults arguing is scary...

740340909.text: Gentlemen, gentlemen! Calm down! There's no need to be upset over such a trifling matter!

740340910.text: This is no trifling matter, Roialte! This is a matter of grave importance that impacts the entire Maison Gestion. I dare not act rashly and decide it on my own!

740340911.text: So it is! There is nothing trivial at all about protecting our secrets. I don't think there is anyone in the whole Maison Gestion more suited to handling this matter than you!

740340912.text: Please, relax! Why must you gentlemen argue about who is in charge? As I see it, there's no need for anyone to be primarily responsible, you don't even need to coordinate.

740340915.text: I fear I do not understand your meaning, Roialte.

740340916.text: I don't quite follow your train of thought, Roialte.

740340917.text: You two are both gentlemen with a wealth of experience, and know that when dealing with something complicated, we must first divide it into simple things.

740340918.text: The responsibility of preventing people from leaking secrets using Kameras should logically fall to Gattineo.

740340946.text: But you need not do anything extra. Just continue catching leakers, as before.

740340919.text: As for informing everyone of the policy that Kameras can't be brought into Maison Gestion, this troubling task must fall to Difor. Nobody else in the Maison Gestion can clarify the new policy to the staff.

740340920.text: We have no capability to enforce it! Nobody listens to us!

740340921.text: *sigh* You don't need to worry about that. Leave enforcement to Gattineo, what you need to do is not "notify," but "propose."

740340922.text: The bigger you print the proposal, the better. Put it at the entrance, and be sure to print the case of the last Kamera leak below it. That should be enough.
